welcome.headline: A place to keep track of what's actually happening to you.
welcome.body: EMBR helps you turn what you're experiencing into something you can look back on, understand, and eventually bring into a conversation with your doctor. It doesn't diagnose you or replace your clinician. It helps you organize your own record, on your own terms.

jobToBeDone.headline: What do you want EMBR to help you with?
jobToBeDone.hint: This just shapes what we show you first. You can always change your mind later.
jobToBeDone.keepRecord: Keep a better record, long term

whatsGoingOn.headline: What have you noticed lately?
whatsGoingOn.hint: Pick anything that's felt different. This isn't a log yet. It just helps your first check-in feel like it already knows you.

appointmentStatus.headline: Do you have a healthcare appointment coming up?
appointmentStatus.hint: No need for the exact date yet. Just helps us know whether to keep BRIEF close at hand.
appointmentStatus.unsureWhen: Yes, but I'm not sure when

theLoop.headline: Here's how EMBR works.
theLoop.trackTreatmentsHint: Treatments you try — HRT, supplements, medication, anything else — can be tracked here too.
theLoop.patternsTitle: Once you've logged for a couple of weeks, you might see something like:
theLoop.patternsExample: "Your sleep disruption appeared alongside lower energy on 6 days."
theLoop.patternsCaveat: Descriptive, not diagnostic. EMBR never tells you what's causing something.
theLoop.briefBody: A structured summary of your record, built when you're ready. Not automatically.
theLoop.conversationTitle: Something concrete to bring into your next appointment.

Dashboard.hotFlashAriaLabel: Log a hot flash happening right now
Dashboard.hotFlashPrompt: Having a hot flash right now?
Dashboard.hotFlashHint: Tap it. That's the whole log entry.
Dashboard.hotFlashConfirmation: Logged. Adjust the severity below if it wasn't moderate.
Dashboard.noLogsYet: Nothing logged yet — use the button above whenever something happens.
Dashboard.thisWeek: {count, plural, one {# log this week} other {# logs this week}}

startingPoint.understandPatterns: You're here to understand patterns. We'll start surfacing them as you log.
startingPoint.prepareForAppointment: You're preparing for a healthcare conversation. Let's help you build something concrete.
startingPoint.keepRecord: Let's start building your record over time.
startingPoint.notSure: Let's see what your record starts to show.

Trends.title: Trends
Trends.noSymptomsYet: Nothing logged in this window yet — patterns will show up here as you go.
Trends.noCycleDataYet: Log at least two period-start days to see cycle lengths here. Irregular or absent cycles are common in perimenopause — this is a record for you and your provider, not a diagnosis.
Trends.averagingDays: Averaging {days} days between period starts over this window.
Trends.irregularityNote: Cycle irregularity is expected during perimenopause — this view is here to help you notice your own pattern, not to flag it as a problem.

CoOccurrence.heading: What you've logged together
CoOccurrence.message: {categoryA} appeared alongside {categoryB} on {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
CoOccurrence.caveat: A description of what you've logged — not a diagnosis, and not a claim about cause.

Organization.title: Organization
Organization.notAMember: You're not part of an organization on EMBR — this page is for the person who administers an employer, insurer, or clinic account.
Organization.notAnAdmin: You belong to an organization, but only its ORG_ADMIN can manage the roster and see aggregate trends. If that should be you, ask your organization's admin to change your role.
Organization.inviteError: Couldn't send that invite — try again.
Organization.noMembersYet: No members yet — send an invite above.
Organization.ssoDescription: Let members at your email domain log in through your identity provider instead of a password. Password login keeps working either way — this doesn't replace it.
Organization.trendsAnonymizedNote: Anonymized across your organization — never any one member's individual record.
Organization.trendsSuppressed: Not enough people have logged symptoms in this window yet to show a trend without risking identifying any one person. This isn't about your organization being too small overall — it's about how many members have actually logged something recently.
Organization.trendsEmpty: Nothing logged across the organization in this window yet.
Organization.basedOnCohort: {count, plural, one {Based on # member} other {Based on # members}} who logged something in this window.

billing.manageDescription: Change your seat count, update your payment method, or view invoices.

Settings.title: Settings
Settings.emailNotVerified: Your email address isn't verified yet.
Settings.resendVerificationSuccess: If your email isn't already verified, a new verification link is on its way.
Settings.changePasswordDescription: Changing your password signs you out everywhere, including this device — you'll need to log back in.
Settings.confirmLogoutAllMessage: Every device, including this one, will be signed out.
Settings.deleteAccountDescription: This permanently deletes your account and everything in it — symptom logs, cycle entries, briefs, and settings. This cannot be undone.

Brief.title: EMBR BRIEF
Brief.description: A summary of your tracked symptoms and cycle data, with questions you can bring to your GP. This is a data summary to help your conversation — not a diagnosis, and not medical advice.
Brief.pickDates: Pick both a start and end date.
Brief.generateError: Couldn't generate a brief — try again.
Brief.questionsForGp: Questions to bring to your GP
Brief.notEnoughCycleData: Not enough period-start entries in this range to compute cycle length.
Brief.averageCycleLength: Average cycle length: {days} days ({count, plural, one {# cycle} other {# cycles}} recorded)
Brief.noTreatmentsInRange: No treatments logged in this range.
Brief.treatmentSafetyNote: This reflects what you've logged. It does not assess whether a treatment is working or make treatment recommendations.
Brief.frequencyComparisonEntry: Reported on {currentCount, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, compared with {previousCount, plural, one {# day} other {# days}} in the previous period.

AcceptInvite.missingToken: This invite link is missing its token — check that you copied the whole link from the email.
AcceptInvite.loginPrompt: Log in or create an EMBR account using the same email this invite was sent to, and you'll come right back here to join.
AcceptInvite.alreadyMemberBody: You're already part of this organization — nothing more to do here.
AcceptInvite.wrongAccountBody: This invitation was sent to a different email address than {email}, the account you're currently signed into. Log out and sign back in with the email the invite was sent to.
AcceptInvite.stayAndGoToDashboard: Stay signed in and go to dashboard

Export.title: Export your data
Export.description: Everything you export stays on your device — nothing is sent anywhere else. Leave the dates blank to export everything.
Export.clinicianSummaryDescription: A short summary formatted for a doctor's visit — symptom frequency, cycle length, treatment history, and the log itself.
Export.symptomLogsDescription: Every symptom entry in the range, one row each — for your own records or another tool.
Export.cycleEntriesDescription: Every cycle entry in the range, one row each.
Export.treatmentsDescription: Every treatment logged in the range, one row each.

Treatments.title: Treatments
Treatments.hint: What you're doing about it — HRT, supplements, medication, or anything else. Not a diagnosis or treatment recommendation, just your own record.
Treatments.fillRequiredFields: Add a name and start date first.
Treatments.pickEndDate: Pick an end date, or leave it marked as ongoing.
Treatments.genericError: Something went wrong. Try again in a moment.
Treatments.impactError: Couldn't load this — try again in a moment.
Treatments.impactInsufficientData: Not enough time has passed since starting to show a comparison yet.
Treatments.impactDisclaimer: A count of how often you logged symptoms, not a measure of whether the treatment is working.
